evidence.curator_note: Substrate as drawn: a 2-alkanone molecular ion printed as C3H7-CH(H)-CH2-CH2-C(=O)-CH3 with the gamma hydrogen on C5 drawn EXPLICITLY and '+.' printed above the carbonyl oxygen. INSTANTIATION of the condensed 'C3H7' label (the page does not draw it out): it is taken as ISOPROPYL, making the compound 6-methyl-2-heptanone. That is not a guess -- the running text introducing this scheme rationalises 'the characteristic peaks in ... 6-methyl-2-heptanone (Figure 9.9)' and names 'a pair of acylium ions (m/z 113 and 43 in Figure 9.9) and a pair of alkyl ions (m/z 85 and 15)', which are exactly this equation's products. n-Propyl would give 2-octanone, an isomer with identical nominal masses at every step, so the drawing alone cannot distinguish them and the text is what settles it. LOCALIZATION (convention B): charge and odd electron are written on the oxygen where the page prints them, [C:2]=[O+:9]. Book draws 0 arc(s) on the molecular ion -- there is no fishhook anywhere on it; every arrow leaving it carries only a label. SECOND channel: an arrow labelled 'alpha' to 'C6H13CO+ / m/z 113'. The complementary alpha cleavage to IMS9-EQ9.26a -- the C1-C2 bond breaks instead, expelling CH3. and keeping the charge on the larger acylium. (The running text calls these 'a pair of acylium ions (m/z 113 and 43)' and notes the more abundant one usually comes from loss of the LARGER alkyl, i.e. m/z 43.) Book draws 0 arc(s); all three moves are curator-supplied, same canonical triple as the other acylium channel. MS CONTEXT: the page prints no ionisation conditions, so 70 eV EI is the corpus house default, disclosed rather than read off the page. Figure 9.9 (printed p247) is the 6-methyl-2-heptanone spectrum and does carry abundances, but it is NOT this page and this scheme prints no percentage, so per convention F no relative_intensity is recorded; peaks are status 'proposed'.

locator.section: 9.3 Aldehydes and ketones ('i' arrow from m/z 113)

evidence.curator_note: The short arrow labelled with an italic 'i' running from m/z 113 down to 'C6H13+ / m/z 85': loss of neutral CO from the acylium. Book draws 0 arc(s) and no structure -- only the formulas -- so the single move is curator-supplied. ENCODING: this is a genuinely heterolytic (2-electron) step from an EVEN-ELECTRON acylium, so it is one double-barbed arrow, not fishhooks -- the C2-C3 bonding pair localises on C2, leaving C3 as the hexyl cation and C2 as the carbon lone pair of :C≡O:. Carbon monoxide is written [C-:2]#[O+:9], the standard charge-separated RDKit form; the fragment is neutral overall.
